{{nihongo|'''Hanifu Shrine'''|波爾布神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Aiba, Shin-Asahi-chō, {{ill|Takashima, Shiga|Q845794|qid=Q845794}}, {{ill|Shiga Prefecture|Q131358|qid=Q131358}}. It is also called Habu Daimyōjin or Habu-san. {{nihongo|'''Hanifu Shrine'''|波爾布神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

== Enshrined deities ==
*{{ill|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Q9285919|qid=Q9285919|lt=Haniyama-hime-no-Mikoto}}
*{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mitsuha-no-me-no-Kami}}

== Shrine crest ==
:Sennari gourd

== History ==
:Founding period is unknown. Shrine tradition says Mitsuha-no-me-no-Mikoto had been worshiped since ancient times, and in {{ill|Tenpyō|Q1199879|qid=Q1199879}} 13, {{ill|Haniyasu-hiko and Haniyasu-hime|Q9285919|qid=Q9285919|lt=Haniyama-hime-no-Mikoto}} was invited from {{ill|Tatsushima Meoyanomikoto Shrine|Q11486644|qid=Q11486644}} in Naka District of {{ill|Awa Province (Tokushima)|Q907457|qid=Q907457}} (present {{ill|Komatsushima, Tokushima|Q823493|qid=Q823493}}, {{ill|Tokushima Prefecture|Q160734|qid=Q160734}}). It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}. It was the sōsha of Kizu-no-shō. In an {{ill|Ōei|Q1193078|qid=Q1193078}} cadastral ledger, over one chō of tax-exempt fields were assigned. During the Meiji-period {{ill|Haibutsu kishaku|Q702298|qid=Q702298}}, many shrine treasures were lost due to radicals in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Takashima Kamui Corps}}. A list of discarded items remains in the "Taya family documents" (included in 'Takashima Gunshi' and '{{ill|Shintō Taikei|Q11590923|qid=Q11590923}} Ōmi Province'). Former {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.

== Festivals ==
:'''Kinen Festival''' March 10
:'''Annual Festival''' April 20
:Until Meiji, it was held on the first {{ill|chǒu|Q16539206|qid=Q16539206}} of the second month.
:Shrine tradition says the sacred object of {{ill|Chikuma Shrine (Maibara)|Q11602835|qid=Q11602835|lt=Chikuma Shrine}} in Irie village, {{ill|Sakata District, Shiga|Q7402853|qid=Q7402853}} (present {{ill|Maibara, Shiga|Q824020|qid=Q824020}}), was carried by rising waters of {{ill|Lake Biwa|Q200239|qid=Q200239}} and washed ashore at Kizu beach, and in connection with that, an offering rite used to cross the lake from Chikuma Shrine. Because of rough waters this crossing rite was abolished, and sacred fields called Chikuma-da were established. Rice from those fields, called '''Chikuma Miké''', came to be offered at the otabisho during mikoshi processions. ("Aiba Village Local History," "Takashima Gunshi")
:The festival was traditionally conducted by shrine families of {{ill|Tatehaya Shrine (Takashima)|Q11387238|qid=Q11387238|lt=Tatesuna Shrine}}, {{ill|Ookuninushi Shrine (Takashima)|Q11433666|qid=Q11433666|lt=Ōkuninushi Shrine}}, and Wakamiya Hachiman-sha; today priests from {{ill|Hiyoshi Ninomiya Shrine|Q11505027|qid=Q11505027}} and Mori Shrine may also join.
:'''Niiname Festival''' November 23
